decks.name: Neuropathology III: Phakomatoses, Degenerative & Metabolic (Board Review)

cards.rueckseite:
Autosomal dominant, **chromosome 17q11 (neurofibromin)**, 1:3,000, ~50% new mutations.
Criteria (≥ 2): **≥ 6 café-au-lait spots** (> 5 mm prepubertal, > 15 mm postpubertal), **≥ 2 neurofibromas or 1 plexiform**, axillary/inguinal **freckling**, **optic pathway glioma**, **≥ 2 Lisch nodules**, distinctive bone lesion (**sphenoid wing dysplasia**, long bone pseudarthrosis), first-degree relative.

Optic pathway gliomas (pilocytic), other low-grade astrocytomas (brainstem), **MPNST** (~5–10%, from plexiform neurofibromas), pheochromocytoma, "UBOs" (T2 hyperintensities in basal ganglia, cerebellum; regress with age), **dural ectasia** with posterior vertebral scalloping, lateral meningoceles, **dystrophic scoliosis**, moyamoya, aqueductal stenosis.

Autosomal dominant, **chromosome 22q12 (merlin/schwannomin)**, 1:25,000–50,000.
Criteria: **bilateral vestibular schwannomas**, or first-degree relative + unilateral VS, or ≥ 2 of meningioma, schwannoma, glioma (ependymoma), neurofibroma, **juvenile posterior subcapsular cataract**.
Tumors: "**MISME**": Multiple Inherited Schwannomas, Meningiomas, Ependymomas (spinal ependymoma in NF2, astrocytoma in NF1). Few café-au-lait spots.

Autosomal dominant: **TSC1 (hamartin, 9q34)**, **TSC2 (tuberin, 16p13)** → mTOR activation.
Classic triad (< 50%): **seizures** (infantile spasms → ACTH/vigabatrin), **intellectual disability**, **facial angiofibromas** ("adenoma sebaceum").
CNS: **cortical tubers**, **subependymal nodules** (calcified, "candle guttering"), **SEGA** at the foramen of Monro (→ hydrocephalus; everolimus or resection).
Other: ash-leaf spots, shagreen patch, ungual fibromas, cardiac **rhabdomyomas**, renal **angiomyolipomas**, pulmonary LAM, retinal hamartomas.

Autosomal dominant, **VHL tumor suppressor on 3p25** (regulates HIF → VEGF/EPO).
**Hemangioblastomas** (cerebellum, brainstem, spinal cord), **retinal hemangioblastomas** (von Hippel tumor), **clear cell renal cell carcinoma** (major cause of death), **pheochromocytoma**, pancreatic/renal cysts and neuroendocrine tumors, **endolymphatic sac tumors**, epididymal cystadenomas. ~25–30% of hemangioblastoma patients have VHL.

**Sporadic** (somatic **GNAQ** mutation), not inherited. Facial **port-wine stain (V1)**, ipsilateral **leptomeningeal venous angiomatosis** (enhancing pia), **"tram-track" gyral calcifications** (parieto-occipital), hemispheric atrophy, enlarged choroid plexus, **glaucoma**. Contralateral seizures, hemiparesis, hemianopia. Refractory epilepsy → hemispherectomy.

Autosomal dominant: **ENG (endoglin, HHT1)**, **ACVRL1/ALK1 (HHT2)** (TGF-β pathway). Epistaxis (most common), mucocutaneous telangiectasias, AVMs of lung, liver, **brain and spinal cord** (often multiple).
Neurologic events often from **pulmonary AVMs** → paradoxical emboli, **brain abscess**. Screen with MRI and contrast echocardiography.

**Wyburn–Mason (Bonnet–Dechaume–Blanc):** unilateral retinal + optic pathway/**midbrain AVMs**, facial vascular nevus; nonhereditary.
**Ataxia–telangiectasia:** autosomal recessive, **ATM** (DNA repair), cerebellar ataxia, oculocutaneous telangiectasias, immunodeficiency, lymphoma/leukemia, radiosensitivity.
**Klippel–Trenaunay:** limb overgrowth, port-wine stain, venous malformations; spinal AVMs.

**Thiamine (B1) deficiency** (alcohol, hyperemesis, bariatric surgery). Triad: **confusion, ophthalmoplegia (nystagmus, VI palsy), ataxia**. Lesions: **mammillary bodies**, medial thalamus, periaqueductal gray, tectum (petechial hemorrhage, T2/DWI). Give **thiamine before glucose**.
Korsakoff: anterograde > retrograde amnesia, **confabulation** (mediodorsal thalamus, mammillary bodies).

**Vitamin B12 deficiency** (pernicious anemia, metformin, nitrous oxide exposure, gastrectomy) or copper deficiency. Demyelination of **dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts** (cervical/upper thoracic): loss of vibration/proprioception, sensory ataxia, spasticity, extensor plantar responses with reduced ankle reflexes (neuropathy). MRI: **inverted-V sign** in the dorsal columns. Also megaloblastic anemia, dementia.

**Central pontine (± extrapontine) myelinolysis** after **rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia**; risks: alcoholism, malnutrition, liver transplant, hypokalemia. Symmetric demyelination of the central pons sparing the periphery ("trident" shape). Clinically: dysarthria, dysphagia, quadriparesis, locked-in, 2–6 days after correction.

cards.vorderseite: Toxic lesions of the globus pallidus and other selective targets
cards.rueckseite:
- **Carbon monoxide:** bilateral **globus pallidus** necrosis, delayed leukoencephalopathy
- **Methanol:** **putaminal** necrosis/hemorrhage, optic nerve (blindness), metabolic acidosis
- **MPTP:** substantia nigra → parkinsonism
- **Manganese:** globus pallidus (T1 hyperintense), parkinsonism
- **Cyanide:** basal ganglia, cortex

zeilen: Metachromatic sulfatide granules, periventricular tigroid pattern, neuropathy
Globoid cells, infantile irritability, optic atrophy, thalami hyperdense
Boys, parieto-occipital enhancing leading edge, adrenal insufficiency
Macrocephaly, NAA peak ↑ on MRS, subcortical U-fibers

cards.rueckseite:
Extracellular **β-amyloid plaques** (neuritic plaques) and intracellular **neurofibrillary tangles** (hyperphosphorylated tau), **granulovacuolar degeneration** and Hirano bodies (hippocampus), amyloid angiopathy (lobar hemorrhage). Atrophy of **hippocampus/entorhinal cortex**, temporoparietal. Loss of cholinergic neurons in **nucleus basalis of Meynert**.
Genetics: APP (21), PSEN1 (14), PSEN2 (1); **APOE ε4** risk.

- **PSP:** tau; midbrain atrophy (**"hummingbird" sign**), vertical gaze palsy (down), axial rigidity, early falls
- **MSA:** α-synuclein **glial cytoplasmic inclusions** (oligodendrocytes); MSA-C: pontine **"hot cross bun"** sign, cerebellar atrophy; MSA-P: putaminal rim; autonomic failure
- **Corticobasal degeneration:** tau, asymmetric parietal atrophy, alien limb, apraxia
- **Lewy body dementia:** cortical Lewy bodies, fluctuations, hallucinations, neuroleptic sensitivity

Autosomal dominant **CAG repeat** expansion in **HTT (chromosome 4p)**, anticipation (paternal). Loss of GABAergic medium spiny neurons in **caudate (head) > putamen** → "box-car" frontal horns. Chorea, psychiatric symptoms, dementia; onset 30–50 y.

cards.vorderseite: ALS: pathology and differential for neurosurgeons
cards.rueckseite:
Combined **upper and lower motor neuron** degeneration (anterior horn cells, corticospinal tracts, Betz cells, motor nuclei except III/IV/VI and Onuf). **Bunina bodies**, TDP-43 inclusions; SOD1, C9orf72. Sensory, bladder and eye movements spared.
Mimic: **cervical spondylotic myelopathy** with radiculopathy (look for sensory signs, bladder, tongue fasciculations/bulbar signs favor ALS).

Perivenular inflammatory demyelination with relative **axonal preservation**, oligodendrocyte loss, gliosis. Plaques periventricular (**Dawson fingers**, perpendicular to ventricles), juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord (< 2 segments, peripheral); active plaques show **open-ring (incomplete) enhancement**. CSF **oligoclonal bands**. **Tumefactive MS** mimics tumor (incomplete ring, little mass effect).

**NMO spectrum:** **aquaporin-4 IgG** (astrocytopathy); severe optic neuritis and **longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (≥ 3 segments)**, area postrema syndrome (hiccups, vomiting); oligoclonal bands usually absent. Treat attacks with steroids/plasma exchange; MS drugs (interferon, natalizumab) can worsen it. MOG-antibody disease is a related entity.

Most vulnerable neurons: **hippocampal CA1 (Sommer sector)**, **cerebellar Purkinje cells**, cortical **layers 3, 5, 6** (**laminar necrosis**), striatum. Watershed infarcts after hypotension (ACA–MCA border: "man in a barrel" proximal arm/leg weakness).

β-amyloid in cortical/leptomeningeal vessel walls (Congo red, apple-green birefringence). Elderly: **recurrent lobar hemorrhages**, cortical **microbleeds** (SWI), convexity SAH, **superficial siderosis** (Boston criteria). Associated with Alzheimer disease, APOE ε2/ε4. Surgery for lobar hematoma possible; avoid anticoagulation.

zeilen: + perineurium (only epineurium intact; neuroma in continuity)
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 331–332. Wallerian degeneration of the distal stump begins within 24–36 h.

cards.rueckseite: Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy after infection (**Campylobacter jejuni**, CMV, EBV, Zika). Ascending weakness, **areflexia**, autonomic instability, respiratory failure. CSF: **albuminocytologic dissociation** (high protein, normal cells). Treatment: **IVIG or plasma exchange** (steroids ineffective). Miller Fisher variant (anti-GQ1b): ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia.

Distal symmetric polyneuropathy (most common), **diabetic amyotrophy** (lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy: painful proximal leg weakness, mimics L3/L4 radiculopathy), thoracic radiculopathy, mononeuropathies (CN III **pupil-sparing**, median, ulnar, peroneal), autonomic neuropathy. Entrapment neuropathies more frequent.

cards.vorderseite: Muscle biopsy: neurogenic vs. myopathic pattern
cards.rueckseite:
**Neurogenic (denervation):** angulated atrophic fibers, **fiber-type grouping** (reinnervation), group atrophy, target fibers.
**Myopathic:** variation in fiber size, central nuclei, necrosis and regeneration, fibrosis, inflammation (polymyositis: endomysial CD8; dermatomyositis: perifascicular atrophy).

Both X-linked recessive, **dystrophin** gene (Xp21).
**Duchenne:** absent dystrophin (frameshift), onset < 5 y, **Gowers sign**, calf pseudohypertrophy, CK ↑↑, wheelchair by ~12 y, cardiomyopathy, scoliosis (spinal fusion).
**Becker:** reduced/abnormal dystrophin (in-frame), later onset, milder.

Autosomal dominant **RYR1** (ryanodine receptor) mutation; triggered by **volatile anesthetics** and **succinylcholine** → uncontrolled Ca²⁺ release: **rising end-tidal CO₂** (earliest sign), tachycardia, rigidity (masseter), hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalemia. Treat: stop triggers, **dantrolene**, cooling, treat hyperkalemia. Associated with central core disease.
